topics.topic: Delivery of the conflict-marker and ignored-name policy values to generated code
questions: The `.sync-conflict-` policy value must become a provider-data constant named through `the imported X constant` (or be kept as a design fact outside the generated specification), rather than reaching generated code only as an inline prose literal.
The conflict-marker policy must name one valid delivery path, normally an imported provider constant for the marker or the closed ignored-name policy.

The `.sync-conflict-` marker and the other code-read ignored-name policy values must be placed in a provider constant and named to generated code as the imported constant, or remain design facts outside the specification instead of being supplied as literals.

quotes:

topics.topic: Placement when an eligible ordinary file and an ignored conflict copy share the same hash
questions: If an ordinary eligible file and an ignored conflict copy have the same content hash, does placement by that hash succeed using the ordinary file, or does the presence of the conflict copy require refusal?
When the requested source hash belongs both to an eligible ordinary file and to an ignored conflict copy, must placement succeed for the ordinary file or fail because a conflict copy has that hash?

quotes: 1. A placement is identified by the project and the SHA-256 of the source content (R0-10).

A name is ignored, in any letter case and at every level of the path, when it begins with a dot or
with `~syncthing~`, ends in `.tmp` or `~`, or contains `.sync-conflict-`, the mark of a Syncthing

topics.topic: Whether conflict-copy classification is name-based or limited to actual Syncthing-created copies
questions: Is every name containing `.sync-conflict-` ignored, including an ordinary user-named file, or is the exception limited to files actually created by Syncthing as conflict copies?

quotes:
A name is ignored, in any letter case and at every level of the path, when it begins with a dot or
with `~syncthing~`, ends in `.tmp` or `~`, or contains `.sync-conflict-`, the mark of a Syncthing
conflict copy (R0-14). Names beginning with a dot include Syncthing's
`.syncthing.*`, `.stfolder` and `.stversions` and the phone's `.trashed-*` files. Ignored names are
not reported, ignored folders are not entered, and symbolic links are neither reported nor followed.
judgement.why: The rule classifies by the name condition itself and therefore ignores every matching name regardless of who created the file.
